sets.title: Law and method changes
sets.what: Changes since 2016 that break year-to-year comparisons.
rows: Voter ID: court-ordered interim remedy (reasonable-impediment declaration) for the Nov 2016 general (Veasey v. Abbott)
In-person ID rules in 2016 differ from 2018+ (SB 5, 2017 codified the declaration); small effect on totals
HB 25 (85R): eliminated straight-party voting; first general without it was Nov 2020
Longer ballots and longer Election Day lines from 2020 on; 2016/2018 ED-vs-EV and roll-off not like-for-like with 2020+
V (bill history: enrolled, signed 06/01/2017); effective date 9/1/2020 R
HB 1888 (86R): temporary branch (rolling/mobile) early-voting sites must keep the main-site hours; ends one-day pop-up EV sites
Fewer short-duration EV sites (campuses, rural) from 2020; county EV pace 2016/2018 vs 2020+ not like-for-like
Governor proclamation extended early voting to 18 days (Tue Oct 13 - Fri Oct 30, 2020); mail-ballot hand delivery limited to one site per county
2020 EV day numbers and days-before-ED do not align with 2016/2018/2022/2024/2026 (12-day windows); compare 2020 only by calendar date or final
V (SOS 2020 daily files start 2020-10-13); proclamation R

SB 1 (87th, 2nd C.S.): ID number (DL/ID or SSN4) required on mail applications and carrier envelopes; online tracker and cure; bans drive-thru and 24-hour voting; sets EV hours; no unsolicited applications
Mail rejection rose from 0.8-1.8% (2016-2020) to 3.4-3.5% (2022-2024) [EAVS]; Harris County 2020 drive-thru/24-hour voting not available since; mail comparisons 2016-2020 vs 2022+ broken
SB 1750 (88R): abolished the county elections administrator in counties of 3.5M+ (Harris); elections moved to the county clerk and tax assessor
Harris County administration change between 2022 and 2024; Harris reporting cadence differs by year
SB 1599 (88R): mail-ballot changes (online cure process, ballot board timing)
HB 1243 (88R): illegal voting raised back to a felony
HB 4 (89th, 2nd C.S.): new congressional map PLANC2333; signed Aug 29, 2025; enjoined Nov 18, 2025 (W.D. Tex.); stayed by SCOTUS Dec 4, 2025 (6-3); district judgment reversed Apr 27, 2026

REDISTRICTING BREAK: every CD comparison to 2018-2024 must be re-fit to the 2026 lines (cd_ev.csv does this for 2022/2024 via precinct re-aggregation) or marked not like-for-like; prior CD results are old geography
V (bill enrolled 09/05/2025) / R (court history, Wikipedia citing supremecourt.gov orders 25A608)

SB 2753 (89R): integrates EV and Election Day voting; EV would run from the 12th day before ED through the day before ED incl. weekends; daily 9-hour minimum; counting from the 4th day before ED. Applies only to elections ordered after the SOS issues the report required by Sec. 32
NOT in effect for Nov 2026: the 2026 SOS calendar has EV Mon Oct 19 - Fri Oct 30 (old 17th-day rule). Break flag for 2028+, not 2026
enacted, conditional, not in effect for 2026
V (statute text and bill history, effective 9/1/25 conditional) / I (not triggered for 2026, from the SOS calendar)
SB 2964 (89R): changes to the opportunity to correct defects on mail ballots (Sec. 86.011)
SB 16 (89R): proof of citizenship to register: passed Senate, died in House (last action: committee report sent to Calendars 05/25/2025)
Nov 4, 2025 constitutional amendment election: 17 propositions, all approved (incl. citizenship requirement to vote, Prop 16)
No 2026 effect on counts; the Nov 2025 ballot is an off-cycle turnout point

Mail receipt deadline unchanged: received by 7 pm ED, or by 5 pm Wed Nov 4 if postmarked by 7 pm ED (Sec. 86.007); upheld nationally by Watson v. RNC (SCOTUS 5-4: postmarked ballots received after ED may be counted)
Late-arriving postmarked mail (and UOCAVA) counted after election night in 2026 as in prior years

Mail eligibility unchanged: 65+, disability, out of county, confinement; annual application for 65+/disabled; no permanent list, no all-mail, no drop boxes (in-person hand delivery of a marked mail ballot only at the clerk office with ID)
Mail is ~5% of Texas ballots; outstanding mail is not the race; 65+ dominate mail (VoteHub: 82.8% of mail returns)
No same-day registration; registration deadline Oct 5, 2026; no universal online registration (DPS-transaction online updates only)
Registration totals frozen at Oct 5; DPS failed to transmit ~600,000 registrations (backlog sent to counties in late Sept/Oct 2026): late-processed registrants may appear in the roll mid-EV

Counting: counties of 100,000+ may begin counting mail ballots at the end of in-person EV (Fri Oct 30); others at polls opening on ED; no results before polls close; local canvass 3rd-11th day after ED (Nov 6-14); state canvass 15th-30th day (Nov 18 - Dec 3); in-person cure by the 6th day after ED (Nov 9)
Election-night order: early in-person + mail reported first at 7 pm, then ED precincts; late mail/UOCAVA after
Tarrant County cut Election Day sites from 316 (2022) to 224 (2026) (3-2 Commissioners Court vote, Sep 1, 2026); court denied restoring sites for 2026 (Oct 13)
Tarrant ED capacity lower than 2022/2024: Tarrant ED share comparisons not like-for-like
Dallas County 2026 primary used party-specific precinct sites on ED (confusion; emergency petition to extend hours)
Primary-history (2026 primary) participation in Dallas may be depressed on ED; affects basis-A primary flags slightly

W.D. Tex. three-judge court enjoins the 2025 map as a racial gerrymander (LULAC v. Abbott)
SCOTUS stays the injunction 6-3; 2025 map used for 2026
SCOTUS reverses the district court judgment (map cleared for 2026)
SD-9 special, round 1: Rehmet (D) 47.6, Wambsganss (R) 35.9, Huffman (R) 16.5
SD-9 special runoff: Rehmet (D) 57.3 - Wambsganss (R) 42.7 in a Trump +17 (2024) seat: D flip, +32 vs 2024 margin
SD-4 special: R 75 - D 25 in a Trump +34 seat: D under-performance -16 vs 2024
TX-18 special (D vs D jungle): Menefee 28.9, Edwards 25.6, Jones 19.1, Montiel (R) 6.7
TX-18 runoff: Menefee 68.9 - Edwards 31.1 (D vs D; not a partisan swing test)
Winter storm closed Harris County EV sites Jan 25-26 (TX-18 runoff); suit to extend EV hours

Primary: R Cornyn 42.0 / Paxton 40.5 / Hunt 13.5 (runoff); D Talarico 52.4 / Crockett 46.2. Democratic primary turnout exceeded Republican for the first time since 2020 (top race D 2,319,187 vs R 2,166,910)
Primary: R Abbott 81.8; D Hinojosa 58.5. Scar flag: none
Primary: incumbent Ag Commissioner Sid Miller (Trump-endorsed) lost to Nate Sheets (Abbott-backed) 52-47: first statewide R incumbent to lose renomination in years
Primary: Huffines won the R comptroller primary (~57%) over acting comptroller Hancock and Craddick
Trump endorses Paxton in the Senate runoff
Runoff: Paxton 63.8 - Cornyn 36.2: sitting senator ousted (scar flag)
Runoff: Bo French beat incumbent RRC Jim Wright 50.6-49.4
Runoffs: Middleton (R) and Nathan Johnson (D) nominated

Campaigns announce negotiations for up to three debates; as of Oct 25 Paxton has accepted none (Talarico accepted 4+; Fox issued a 5th invitation; Trump and others urged Paxton to debate in early Oct)
Republican first-ever midterm national convention, Dallas (Sep 9-10); Paxton later privately said it had a negative effect
Talarico attacks AG office handling of the Adam Hoffman child-abuse plea deal (June); Crockett declined to commit to campaign for Talarico; Cornyn declined to fundraise for Paxton
Two former Republican Texas Supreme Court justices (Hankinson, Phillips) endorse Democrat Nathan Johnson
Abbott has declined four debate invitations (first gubernatorial race without a debate since 2010); on day 1 of EV Hinojosa sued Abbott under the Public Information Act over Musk emails
Railroad Commission forum, Dallas Press Club
Tarrant County votes 3-2 to cut ED sites 316 -> 224 (a year after halving EV sites); suit filed Oct 2; relief denied Oct 13
DPS failed to transmit ~200,000 (Sept report) then ~600,000 (Oct) voter registrations to counties after the TEAM overhaul; LWV/MOVE Texas sued Oct 9
LULAC et al. sue over the SAVE-based noncitizen voter purge (NVRA); SOS motion to dismiss June 10, 2026; pending
NFB of Texas sues Harris County over inaccessible mail ballots (ADA)
Jolt Initiative sues AG Paxton over intimidation of its voter-registration work (First Amendment); pending
Watson v. RNC decided 5-4: mail ballots postmarked by ED and received after may be counted (Texas next-day rule stands)
AdImpact: through 9/30 Republicans +$61M aired in Texas Senate; Talarico campaign aired $59M; R broadcast spend +44% but airings only +8%; future reservations largest gap of any battleground (R +80%)
